provenance.paper: Marques-Silva, J. P., & Sakallah, K. A. (1999). GRASP: a search algorithm for propositional satisfiability.
provenance.citation: Marques-Silva, J. P., & Sakallah, K. A. (1999). IEEE Transactions on Computers, 48(5), 506-521.
provenance.locus: Section 3 (conflict analysis): resolving the conflicting clause backwards along antecedent assignments yields a learned conflict clause; non-chronological backtracking to the asserting level.
provenance.notes: Pigeonhole PHP(3,2): 3 pigeons, 2 holes — variables p_ij = pigeon i in hole j numbered 1..6 (p11=1, p12=2, p21=3, p22=4, p31=5, p32=6). Provably UNSAT, and no resolution-free (pure DPLL backtrack-only) trace can avoid conflicts: GRASP-style learning must fire at least one learned clause before refutation.

expected.notes: PHP(3,2) is the canonical UNSAT family; the solver must learn at least one conflict clause (each learn-clause trace step carries the resolution certificate from=/pivots= for independent re-derivation).
